name: Airbus AS365 Dauphin / MH-65 Dolphin
summary: Sleek medium twin with a Fenestron tail and retractable gear; in the US it is best known as the Coast Guard's orange-and-white short-range rescue helicopter, with some civil EMS examples.

wings: Four-blade main rotor on a Starflex hub
engines: Two engines side by side on the roof behind the mast
Two exhausts at the back of the engine cowling
fuselage: Streamlined teardrop fuselage with a pointed nose
Retractable tricycle gear with main wheels pulling into the lower fuselage
Coast Guard: orange-red with a white stripe, rescue hoist above the cabin door, nose FLIR/radar
tail: Shrouded Fenestron in a tall swept fin

tellTales: Sleek twin on wheels with a shrouded fan in a tall swept fin
Orange-and-white Coast Guard paint with a hoist over the door
Small pointed nose and short cabin

confusedWith.howToTell: The Jayhawk is far bigger with an open canted tail rotor; the Dolphin is smaller with a shrouded Fenestron.
The H135 sits on skids with clamshell doors; the Dauphin has retractable wheels and a sleeker pointed nose.
The S-76 has an open four-blade tail rotor and a longer pointed nose; the Dauphin has a Fenestron.
The EC155 has a five-blade rotor and a longer cabin with an extra window; the Dauphin has four blades and a shorter body.
The H160 has curved Blue Edge blade tips, a canted fenestron and a sleeker body; the Dauphin has a four-blade rotor and a straight fenestron.

usCount.source: USCG 84 MH-65E (Navy League Seapower Almanac 2026) + ~28 FAA-registered civil AS365
